references.text: Sins committed in ignorance or by error require atonement, a theme introduced here and elaborated on in chapter 5.
The immediate context describing the guilt offering with an unblemished male sheep from the flock and the priest's atonement.
Continuation of the laws concerning the guilt offering with a ram as the sacrifice and the priest making atonement for forgiveness.
Detailed regulations regarding the guilt offering (אָשָׁם) and the priest's role in atonement.
Offering for unintentional sins committed in ignorance, with a promise of forgiveness.
The priest makes atonement (וְכִפֶּר) and the person receives forgiveness (וְנִסְלַח), the same structure as in 5:18.
The priest makes atonement and the individual receives forgiveness, with parallel language and theological content.
Hebrews refers to an atoning sacrifice for sins committed in ignorance and points to Christ's perfect offering.
The requirement for an unblemished animal (תָּמִים) from the flock (מִן־הַצֹּאן) for the offering.
The requirement for unblemished animals so that the offering may be accepted by the Lord.
